origins: Looking back on yelling, divorce, absence, addiction, neglect, or hard years, some parents decide the damage is permanent. Guilt can be especially heavy when a child is hurting now and we can see the connection. Shame then says, “It is too late and they are broken because of me.”
teaches: God speaks of restoration: “I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts.” The Lord says, “Keep your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for the reward for your work will come… So there is hope for your future, declares the LORD, and your children will return.” Paul writes that “if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation,” and Joseph told his brothers, “what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good.” This is not a denial of real harm. It is a promise that God can redeem what we cannot, and that repentance, repair, and prayer can change a story that is not finished.
self_statements: I cannot undo what I did.
My children are hurt because of me.
It is too late to make it right.
errors: Treating real harm as irreversible ruin.
Predicting that my children will never recover.
Feeling terrible and concluding the damage is total.
questions: What specifically do I believe I did, and what is the actual impact on each child?
Have I acknowledged it to my children, and how did they respond?
What strengths and good memories do my children also have?
What does God say about restoring lost years?
What can I do now to repair, listen, and love?
What is not in my control?
truth: I have made real mistakes, and some have hurt my children. But I have not ruined them beyond God’s ability to restore. I can repent, repair what I can, listen, and pray, trusting God to redeem what I cannot.
hw_truths: God can restore the years the locusts have eaten.
There is hope for my future and my children’s.
God can turn evil to good.
I am a new creation in Christ.
log: Each week, record one step of repair, such as an apology, a listening conversation, or a prayer.
actions: Write what happened without exaggerating or minimizing.
Tell each child what you are sorry for, then listen.
Consider family counseling or a pastor if needed.
Ask God to restore what was lost.
prayer: Father, I carry deep regret over how I have hurt my children. Forgive me, give me courage to repair what I can, and redeem what I cannot. Restore the years that were lost. Amen.
hw_questions: What is the impact on each child?
What strengths do my children have?
What can I trust to God?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God can restore the years that were lost.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I have ruined my children.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
